source.title: Topological Open Problems in the Geometry of Banach Spaces

accepted.question_text: Let X and Y be normed spaces. Characterize the nonlinear maps Φ:X→Y with the following transfer property: whenever Y admits a Kadec norm, X also admits a Kadec norm; and whenever Y admits a strictly convex norm, X also admits a strictly convex norm. Here a Kadec norm is a norm for which the weak topology and the norm topology coincide on the unit sphere, and a strictly convex norm is one whose unit sphere contains no nontrivial line segment.
accepted.context_brief: Nonlinear transfer of Kadec and strictly convex norms

evidence.quote: Let us remember that a norm in a normed space is said to be a Kadec norm if the weak and the norm topologies coincide on the unit sphere, and it is said to be strictly convex when the unit sphere doest not contain any non trivial segments.
Question 1. The study of non linear maps Φ : X → Y transferring a Kadec (resp. a strictly convex) norm from a normed space Y with Kadec (resp. strictly convex) norm to X.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a normed space and let F be a norming subspace of X*. Suppose the identity map from X with the weak topology σ(X,F) to X with its norm topology is σ-continuous, meaning that it is a norm-pointwise limit of maps which are weak-to-norm continuous after countably many domain splittings. Must there exist an equivalent σ(X,F)-Kadec norm ||| · ||| on X, meaning a norm whose unit sphere has the same σ(X,F) and norm topologies?
accepted.context_brief: Convexifying a σ-continuous identity into a Kadec norm

evidence.quote: A norm pointwise limit of a sequence of piecewise continuous maps is called a σ-continuous map, [19].

Question 2. Let X be a normed space and F a norming subspace of X∗ such that the identity map Id : (X, σ(X, F)) → (X, k · k) is σ-continuous. Is it possible to convexify the construction above to get an equivalent σ(X, F)-Kadec norm ||| · |||; i.e., the σ(X, F) and norm topologies coincide on the unit sphere {x ∈ X : |||x||| = 1} ?

accepted.question_text: Are descriptive Banach spaces exactly the σ-fragmented Banach spaces, or is one of these two classes strictly larger? In this setting, a descriptive Banach space is a Banach space whose norm topology has a network that is the countable union of subfamilies which are isolated or discrete in their union for the weak topology.

evidence.quote: the norm topology has a network N that can be written as a countable union of subfamilies, N = ∪∞ n=1Nn, where every one of the subfamilies Nn is a discrete family in its union ∪{N : N ∈ Nn} endowed with the weak topology, i.e., it is an isolated subfamily for the weak topology. No example is known of a Banach space with this kind of network, which is called a descriptive Banach space, and without equivalent Kadec norm
Question 3. Is there any gap between the classes of descriptive Banach spaces and that of σ-fragmented Banach spaces?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a weakly Čech-analytic Banach space in which every norm-open set is a countable union of sets that are differences of weakly closed sets. Must the identity map from X with its weak topology σ(X,X*) to X with its norm topology be σ-continuous, meaning a norm-pointwise limit of maps that are weak-to-norm continuous after countably many domain splittings?
accepted.context_brief: Weakly Čech-analytic spaces with norm-open weak Borel structure

evidence.quote: A norm pointwise limit of a sequence of piecewise continuous maps is called a σ-continuous map, [19].

Question 4. Let X be a weakly Cech analytic Banach space where every norm open set is a countable union of sets which are differences of closed sets for the weak topology. Doest it follow that the identity map Id : (X, σ(X, X∗)) → (X, k · k) is σ-continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space with the Radon-Nikodym property, meaning every bounded closed convex subset of X has slices of arbitrarily small diameter. Must X admit an equivalent Kadec norm? Must X admit an equivalent rotund, equivalently strictly convex, norm?
accepted.context_brief: Radon-Nikodym property and Kadec or rotund renorming

evidence.quote: Question 5. If the Banach space X has the Radon Nikodym property (i.e., every bounded closed convex subset of X has slices of arbitrarily small diameter), does it follow that X has an equivalent Kadec norm? Does it have an equivalent rotund norm?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space with a Fréchet differentiable norm, let S_X be its unit sphere, and let δ:S_X→X* be the duality map satisfying δ(x)(x)=1=||x|| for every x in S_X. Can one construct a sequence of σ-continuous maps φ_p:X*→X, continuous for the norm topologies in the σ-continuous sense, such that the maps φ_p∘δ approximate the identity map on S_X, for example by ensuring that for every x∈S_X, 0 lies in the weak closure of {(Id−φ_p)^n(x): n,p∈N}?
accepted.context_brief: Approximating the identity via duality-map compositions

evidence.quote: δ : (SX, σ(X, X∗)) → X∗ be the duality map; i.e., δ(x)(x) = 1 = kxk for every x ∈ SX.

Question 6. Let X be a Banach space with a Fréchet differentiable norm. Is it possible to construct a sequence of σ-continuous maps for the norm topologies φp : X∗ → X such that the sequence {φp ◦ δ : p ∈ N} will provide a way to approximate the identity map on the unit sphere of X? For instance, in such a way that: 0 ∈ {(Id − φp)n(x) : n, p ∈ N} σ(X,X∗) for every x ∈ SX (see Theorem 3).

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X has a Fréchet differentiable norm, must X admit an equivalent locally uniformly rotund norm? A norm is locally uniformly rotund when, for every sequence x_n and point x, the condition 2||x||^2+2||x_n||^2−||x+x_n||^2→0 implies ||x−x_n||→0.

evidence.quote: A norm k · k in a real vector space X is said to be locally uniformly rotund (LUR) if, asymptotically, it has a local behavior similar to the parallelogram law: limn (2kxk2 + 2kxnk2 − kx + xnk2) = 0 ⇒ limnkx − xnk = 0 for any sequence (xn) and x in X.
Question 7. Let X be a Banach space with a Fréchet differentiable norm. Does it follow that X admits an equivalent locally uniformly rotund norm?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a separable Rosenthal compact space, meaning a compact space of Baire-one functions on a Polish space. Must the Banach space C(K) of continuous scalar-valued functions on K admit an equivalent locally uniformly rotund renorming?
accepted.context_brief: LUR renorming of C(K) for separable Rosenthal compacta

evidence.quote: The former result fits in the study of compact spaces K ⊂ RΓ formed with Baire one functions on a Polish space Γ, the so called Rosenthal compacta.
Question 8. If K is a separable Rosenthal compact then does it follow that C(K) admits an equivalent locally uniformly rotund renorming?

accepted.question_text: Let Γ be a Polish space and let K⊂R^Γ be a compact set of Baire-one functions such that every function in K has at most countably many discontinuities. For C(K), do the Borel sets generated by the pointwise topology and by the supremum norm topology coincide? Is the identity map from C(K) with the pointwise topology to C(K) with the supremum norm σ-continuous? Does C(K) admit an equivalent locally uniformly rotund norm?
accepted.context_brief: Pointwise Borel structure and LUR renorming for Baire-one compacta

evidence.quote: Question 9. Let K ⊂ RΓ be a compact subset of Baire one functions on a Polish space Γ such that every function of K has at most countably many discontinuities. Do the Borel sets for the pointwise and the norm topologies coincide in C(K)? Is the identity map Id : Cp(K) → (C(K), k · k∞) σ-continuous? Does the Banach space C(K) admit an equivalent LUR norm?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a normed space and suppose that, for every ε>0, X can be written as a countable union X=∪_{n=1}∞ X_{n,ε} such that for every x∈X_{n,ε} there is a σ(X,F)-open half-space H containing x for which a chosen measure of noncompactness of H∩X_{n,ε} is less than ε. Replace the Kuratowski index α in this condition by one of the indices λ, β, or χ, where β measures distance to a uniform Eberlein compact set, χ measures distance to a weakly compact set, and λ measures coverability by countably many small-diameter sets. Under any of these three replacement hypotheses, do the norm-Borel and weak-Borel sets of X coincide? Is the identity map from X with its weak topology σ(X,X*) to X with the norm topology σ-continuous? Does X admit an equivalent locally uniformly rotund norm, and, if so, what corresponding network characterizations hold?
accepted.context_brief: Replacing Kuratowski noncompactness in LUR criteria

evidence.quote: Theorem 6. (See [5]) Let X be a normed space and let F be a norming subspace of its dual. Then X admits an equivalent σ(X, F)-lower semi-continuous LUR norm if, and only if, for every ε > 0 we can write X = ∪∞ n=1 Xn,ε in such a way that for every x ∈ Xn,ε, there exists a σ(X, F)-open half space H containing x with α (H ∩ Xn,ε) < ε.

β(B) := inf{ε > 0 : B ⊆ K + εBX where K is a uniform Eberlein compact}. Another one is the distance to a weakly compact subset of the normed space: χ(B) := inf{ε > 0 : B ⊆ K + εBX where K is a weakly compact subset}, or the separability index measuring the distance to separable subsets: λ(B) := inf{ε > 0 : B ⊆ ∪∞ i=1Ai such that diam(Ai) ≤ ε}.

Question 10. Given a normed space X that verifies the conditions of Theorem 6 with the index λ (resp. β, χ) instead of α. Is it true that the Borel sets for the norm and the σ(X, X∗) topology coincide? Is the identity map Id : (X(σ(X, X∗)) → (X, k · k) σ-continuous? Doest X admit an equivalent LUR norm? In case of positive answers to any of the above questions what can be said for the network characterizations?
